result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_bipartite()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if graph is bipartite (2-colorable). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4001-L4054){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_bipartite() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A graph is bipartite if its nodes can be divided into two independent sets such that every edge connects nodes from different sets. Equivalently, the graph can be colored with two colors such that no adjacent nodes share a color. All trees and forests are bipartite. Graphs with odd-length cycles are not. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is bipartite, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A simple path can always be 2-colored by alternating colors along the chain, so it's bipartite: ::: {#f8d8d9b9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) graph.is_bipartite() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: A triangle forces two adjacent nodes to share a color, since an odd-length cycle can never be 2-colored: ::: {#a51248e2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} triangle = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") # closes an odd-length cycle ) triangle.is_bipartite() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: :::
